## Idea

### Content funnel: top, middle, bottom
<a id="growth-content-funnel"></a>

Top of funnel gets attention and may not mention the product ("raises the floor"); middle educates about you; bottom exists to sell or sign up and gets low views.

> It's there to raise the floor of all your content.

`idea` · formats: reel30, reel60, reel90, yt-short, yt-long, carousel, story, podcast · niches: all · stated · from [L07](../sources/L07.md)

### Weekly mix 4 : 2 : 1
<a id="growth-weekly-4-2-1"></a>

4 top-of-funnel high-TAM posts with a through-line, 2 middle-of-funnel "blow their mind" blueprints, 1 bottom-of-funnel "sneak peek inside" (client journey, wins, community Q&A).

> The main goal at the middle of funnel is to blow their mind.

`idea` · formats: reel30, reel60, reel90, yt-short, carousel · niches: all · stated · from [L08](../sources/L08.md) · ⚠ [C18](../clashes.md#c18)

### Series get the best view-to-follower ratio
<a id="growth-series-view-to-follower"></a>

Series ("day one of doing X") get the best view-to-follower ratio; days can be skipped, add value, blend in your expertise, raise the stakes, end with "follow along". Caleb: think like Netflix.

### Monthly franchise and a running storyline
<a id="growth-monthly-franchise"></a>

"₹X PC Build – October 2026" labels make refreshable monthly franchises; a repeated storyline ("prices rising weekly, we're cooked") gives each reel a reason to exist this week.

> This gives every build reel a reason to exist *this week* and makes the series feel like live news

### 70 / 20 / 10 proven, iterate, experiment
<a id="growth-70-20-10"></a>

70% proven content, 20% small iterations (new hook, CTA or format on the same subject), 10% pure experiments.

> This is the bread and butter

### Lead-magnet CTA over a recap strip
<a id="l11-lead-magnet-recap-cta"></a>

CTA: "If you want a list of 100 proven viral hooks just like these, comment the word hook and I'll send them to you for free", over a sideways-scrolling strip of every example clip, '100 PROVEN VIRAL HOOKS' and a glowing yellow 'HOOK'. Caption: '(No emails)'. Result at download: 5,564 comments on 8,070 likes.

**How:** Offer the bigger version of what the reel taught (e.g. '50 gym hooks', 'my full PC settings list'), recap the reel's examples in a scrolling strip under the CTA, and say what they will NOT have to do ('no email').

> comment the word hook and I'll send them to you for free

## Analyse

### Keyword CTA: ~10× more comments
<a id="growth-keyword-cta-comment-gap"></a>

Rahul's keyword-CTA reels got 4–26% comments per like (median ≈ 13%); his one no-CTA reel got 1.3% (88 comments on 256K plays). n = 1, but the clearest natural experiment in the sample.

> That is a ~10× gap. It is the clearest natural experiment in the sample.

`analyse` · formats: reel30, reel60, reel90, yt-short · niches: all, tech · observed · from [R1](../sources/R1.md) · ⚠ [C1](../clashes.md#c1)

### Follower-first: ghost followers, non-follower %
<a id="growth-follower-first-ghosts"></a>

New posts go to followers first; off-topic followers scroll past and stall reach. Check non-follower view % on the last 5–10 posts: above ~50% is probably fine.

> on Instagram, it's a follower first platform

### Viral For You = 4–5× your baseline
<a id="growth-viral-for-you"></a>

Viral is relative: about 4–5× your own baseline (500 views → 2,000 is viral for you); then the baseline climbs.

> I call it viral for you. VFY

### Multiplier sheet: score posts vs median
<a id="growth-multiplier-sheet"></a>

Per platform and format, benchmark = median of the last 75–90 days; report each post as a multiple (150K ÷ 100K = 1.5×) after ~11 days; update the benchmark monthly; share across platforms.

**How:** Google Sheets: MEDIAN over the last 90 days per format; post views ÷ median.

> directionally correct, not scientifically accurate

<a id="growth-top-10-percent-review"></a>

Take the last 90 days (or 30), find the top 10% and what occurred in all of them (usually one or two things); learn from the top, not the bottom; redo monthly.

### Untangle: hook, format, topic, illustration
<a id="growth-untangle-data"></a>

Split each week's videos into hook (psychological principle), format (visual form), topic (one word) and illustration (metaphor, story, stat, quote); test each part separately the next week.

> You improve your content by untangling data.

### Track only metrics that change actions
<a id="growth-track-few-metrics"></a>

Track 2–4 metrics that change what you do next; optimise for conversions (sales, leads, hires) over likes. Caleb would take 30–40% fewer views for a higher conversion rate.

> if it doesn't change your actions, don't track it

### Pillar system: 3–5 formats × 3–4 a month
<a id="growth-pillar-system"></a>

Test 3–5 formats, each 3–4 times a month (12–16 posts); review views, saves, shares, hook rate and new vs old followers a couple of days after month end (~1 h); swap a format after two worse months.

> every business should have, in my opinion, between three and five formats you're testing.
